column1: In the EV3's dual-processor architecture, why does user bytecode entering an infinite loop not disrupt motor control?
column2: The ARM9 processor (running user program logic) is separated from a dedicated AVR coprocessor that handles all ADC sensor conversion and PWM motor control, so real-time timing integrity is preserved regardless of main CPU bottlenecks.

column1: Of the EV3's 64 MB RAM, roughly how much is reserved for OS kernel/drivers vs. available to user programs?
column2: ~30 MB is reserved for the OS kernel and device drivers, leaving roughly 34 MB of working memory for user programs.

column1: What memory-management discipline does the EV3's constrained RAM budget force on program design?
column2: Minimize dynamic allocation, reuse buffers across sensor reads, avoid recursion that exhausts the stack, use circular buffers instead of unbounded arrays, and prefer fixed-point arithmetic over floating-point.

column1: What is the key architectural difference between NXT and EV3 sensor communication layers?
column2: NXT uses 10-bit ADC analog inputs sampled at ~1 kHz plus RS-485 for digital sensors; EV3 uses a fully digital UART sensor bus at 460,800 baud, alongside legacy I²C and analog paths.

column1: How does the EV3 touch sensor electrically determine 'pressed' vs 'released'?
column2: It acts as a voltage divider; the firmware compares the sampled ADC voltage against a threshold (~2.5V on a 5V rail) to decide pressed (circuit closed/open) vs released.

column1: What is the core misconception about Mindstorms motor control that first-principles actuator theory corrects?
column2: That setting a motor's power level directly produces predictable motion. In reality, torque varies nonlinearly with angular velocity, load shifts dynamically, and transmission compliance/backlash/friction corrupt the ideal command-to-displacement relationship.

column1: How does quadrature encoding in EV3/SPIKE motors determine rotation direction?
column2: Two phase-shifted channels (A and B, 90° offset) are compared: if channel A leads channel B, rotation is forward; if B leads A, rotation is reverse.

column1: What is the EV3 motor torque-speed relationship formula, and what does each term represent?
column2: τ = τ_stall − k_v·ω, where τ is instantaneous torque, τ_stall is stall (zero-velocity) torque, k_v is the motor's velocity constant, and ω is angular velocity in rad/s.

column1: What are the approximate stall torques of the EV3 Large Motor and Medium Motor?
column2: Large Motor: ~0.4 Nm stall torque; Medium Motor: ~0.12 Nm stall torque.

column1: What is the central invariant of Finite State Machine (FSM) design in robot programming?
column2: The robot occupies exactly one state at any given moment, making the question 'what state is the machine in?' sufficient to fully explain current behavior—making hidden state explicit and debuggable.

State: a named behavior configuration (e.g., LINE_FOLLOW). Transition: a directed edge between states guarded by a condition. Event: a sensory change (sensor trigger, timer expiry) that can trigger a transition. Action: work done on entering, during, or on exiting a state (entry/do/exit action).

column1: In the two-wheeled differential drive chassis build, why is 5-12-13 Pythagorean triangulation used for the diagonal brace, and why support the outboard wheel axle with a bushing?
column2: Triangulation locks frame geometry against torque reaction from drive motors, converting shear loads into tension/compression instead of bending pin connections. Outboard axle support (dual-supported wheel) eliminates radial runout that otherwise causes sinusoidal odometry errors in single-supported drives.
